title: The 09:30–10:00 range, candle by candle
definition: This is a timed high–low range. Start at 09:30 New York, wait thirty minutes, then extend the completed boundaries.

steps.title: 1 · The window starts
steps.explanation: Only the opening candle is revealed. The final high and low are still unknown.

steps.title: 2 · Freeze at 10:00
steps.explanation: Thirty completed candles define the range. Match each number below to its coloured line.

steps.title: 3 · Reveal the later movement
steps.explanation: The reference stays fixed while later candles unfold; a break alone is not an entry.

title: Midnight range: measure 00:00–00:30
definition: This is a timed range, not a reopening gap. The blue column marks the thirty-minute observation window in New York time.

steps.title: 1 · Start at midnight
steps.explanation: Look at the 00:00 candle. The later prices are hidden; no final range has been drawn.

steps.title: 2 · Complete thirty minutes
steps.explanation: The high, low and midpoint now appear together. These are measured from 00:00 through the completed 00:29 candle.

steps.title: 3 · Watch price against the fixed range
steps.explanation: The later candles test or leave the reference. The box does not move to fit the outcome.

title: RTH gap: yesterday’s close versus the next open
definition: Overnight candles are deliberately omitted. This example declares a 09:30–16:15 RTH template: the 16:14 candle close is the previous reference, not exchange settlement.

steps.title: 1 · Save the previous close
steps.explanation: The final 16:14 candle supplies the selected closing reference.

steps.title: 2 · Compare the next 09:30 open
steps.explanation: The shaded interval connects two prices across the omitted overnight period. It is not the first half-hour’s trading range.

steps.title: 3 · Follow the actual retest
steps.explanation: An edge test, midpoint touch and full traversal are different. Read the candle lows and highs against the labelled lines.

title: Weekly gap reference on daily candles
definition: This daily feed compares Friday’s close with the following Monday-labelled bar’s open. It shows the reference geometry, not the first Sunday tick or the order of intraday tests. Verify the exact opening quote in your own session feed.

steps.title: 1 · Save Friday’s closing reference
steps.explanation: The last completed Friday supplies one boundary.

steps.title: 2 · Add the next opening reference
steps.explanation: The two daily feed references define the shaded interval and its midpoint.

steps.title: 3 · Keep the daily-view limitation
steps.explanation: Daily wicks can show a level was reached; they cannot establish the exact intraday sequence or an executable order.

title: Three real candles: measure before qualifying
definition: The interval uses candle 1 and candle 3 wicks. This is a geometric candidate; the balanced-range filter and complete entry model still require separate assessment.

steps.title: 1 · Candle 3 is not complete
steps.explanation: No final FVG interval is shown before the third candle closes.

steps.title: 2 · Measure the completed gap
steps.explanation: Match the outer-wick boundaries to the coloured lines. CE is their arithmetic midpoint.

steps.title: 3 · Observe the later outcome
steps.explanation: Compare the actual return with the edge and CE. Neither the label nor an edge touch proves a filled midpoint order.

title: Twenty completed sessions, one fixed range
definition: The first twenty daily candles form the declared lookback. Later candles are separate. Premium and discount refer only to these visible anchors.

steps.title: 1 · Complete the lookback
steps.explanation: The highest high and lowest low of these twenty completed sessions set the boundaries.

steps.title: 2 · Reveal the next session
steps.explanation: Compare the new price with the already fixed midpoint; do not move the range to fit it.

steps.title: 3 · Keep the anchors unchanged
steps.explanation: Range location supplies context; it does not automatically choose an entry or guarantee a reaction.

title: ES breaks its high first; NQ catches up
definition: The two charts share minute timestamps. Each blue line is that instrument’s own 08:00–09:30 high. Compare each market with its own anchor, not the other market’s price.

steps.title: 1 · Save both premarket highs
steps.explanation: Both anchors are known before the cash open.

steps.title: 2 · 09:30: ES exceeds its high
steps.explanation: ES has exceeded its premarket high; NQ has not. This is a high-based non-confirmation at this time.

steps.title: 3 · 09:37: NQ also exceeds its high
steps.explanation: Both prior highs have now been exceeded. The earlier continuing-divergence claim must be removed.

title: Old high, excursion and response
definition: The line is a measured premarket high, not visible proof of hidden stops. Follow the candle closes before naming the response.

steps.title: 1 · Mark the known high
steps.explanation: The reference was known before the later excursion.

steps.title: 2 · Observe a close above it
steps.explanation: The break is visible. The subsequent response is still hidden.

steps.title: 3 · Reveal the response
steps.explanation: Observe the return below the prior high. This alone does not prove institutional intent or a filled Turtle Soup entry.

title: Venom context: range before response
definition: The box is the completed 08:00–09:30 range. These real one-minute candles show a close above its high and a later opposing response. This is not a verified Venom execution or a claim that a deferred order filled.

steps.title: 1 · Freeze the pre-open range
steps.explanation: Both boundaries are known as the cash opening period begins.

steps.title: 2 · Reveal the opening excursion
steps.explanation: At 09:37 the completed candle closes above the pre-open high. Inspect its body and close, not only the wick.

steps.title: 3 · Reveal the opposing response
steps.explanation: By the completed 09:55 candle, price has moved below the pre-open low. That movement still does not prove an entry or fill.

title: A post-10:00 swing needs confirmation
definition: This exercise uses an explicit three-candle swing-high test to explain confirmation delay. Choosing a prominent swing for a broader lunch model remains a separate judgment.

steps.title: 1 · The central high is visible
steps.explanation: The right-hand candle is not complete, so the swing is not confirmed.

steps.title: 2 · Complete the right-hand candle
steps.explanation: Both neighbouring highs are lower. The declared three-candle test now confirms the reference.

steps.title: 3 · Observe what follows
steps.explanation: Later prices cannot justify placing the confirmed label before its recognition time.

title: The afternoon has its own range
definition: Measure 13:30–14:00 separately. A new time window does not automatically reverse the morning.

steps.title: 1 · Start at 13:30
steps.explanation: The final afternoon boundaries remain unknown.

steps.title: 2 · Freeze at 14:00
steps.explanation: Six completed five-minute candles define this separate range.

steps.title: 3 · Compare later movement
steps.explanation: The fixed reference organises observation; the clock does not predict a reversal.

title: FOMC: two scheduled information events
definition: Actual NQ five-minute candles from 16 September 2026. The statement was scheduled for 14:00 and the press conference for 14:30 New York. Timing alone does not prove a single cause for every price move.

steps.title: 1 · Before the statement
steps.explanation: The calendar is known, but the response is not.

steps.title: 2 · Reveal the statement period
steps.explanation: The 14:00–14:25 candles are visible. The later press-conference response is hidden.

steps.title: 3 · Reveal the later period
steps.explanation: Compare the later candles without assuming reversal or guaranteed execution. OHLC does not resolve every intrabar order.

title: Reveal the week one completed day at a time
definition: The first candle is the completed prior Friday. Later candles reveal the new week. Friday’s final chart must not supply Monday’s decision.

steps.title: 1 · Only the prior Friday is known
steps.explanation: The new weekly extremes do not exist yet.

steps.title: 2 · After Monday closes
steps.explanation: Monday’s full range is now available, not before its close.

steps.title: 3 · After the week completes
steps.explanation: Describe the completed week without projecting that knowledge backwards.

title: Index movement is not an option payoff
definition: These are actual S&P 500 index candles, not option quotes. They provide underlying context only. Strike, premium, expiry and settlement remain separate contract inputs.

steps.title: 1 · Observe the underlying
steps.explanation: An index candle does not tell you the option premium.

steps.title: 2 · Reveal later sessions
steps.explanation: Direction alone does not establish an option’s profit or loss.

steps.title: 3 · Keep contract arithmetic separate
steps.explanation: The payoff calculator below uses explicitly hypothetical terms, not historical option prices.

title: Write your decision before revealing the next candles
definition: A real chart observation is not a filled trade. Keep no-entry, unfilled and ambiguous outcomes in the journal.

steps.title: 1 · State what is known
steps.explanation: Write the reference, timeframe and information still missing.

steps.title: 2 · Record the decision before continuing
steps.explanation: Use this lesson’s personal notes. Define an entry condition and a reason to skip before seeing later candles.

steps.title: 3 · Review without changing the original
steps.explanation: Compare the result with the original note. Do not count a directional idea as a filled trade without evidence.
